newsitem.title: USA: US price stability "doing very well" -- Fed's Rivlin.
newsitem.headline: US price stability "doing very well" -- Fed's Rivlin.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board vice chairman Alice Rivlin said on Wednesday that price stability in the U.S. economy is doing very well.
"We're certainly doing very well at the moment," Rivlin told reporters here, referring to price stability in the United States.
She said, however, the debate now centers on how to maintain prices at desired levels. "The problem is to stay there," Rivlin told journalists after addressing a group of international bankers.
Rivlin said the gap between U.S. skilled and non-skilled workers has widened, indicating that over time the latter have fallen behind.

"Over time what's happened is that the gap has widened and people without skills have fallen not just relatively but absolutely behind," Rivlin said, responding to a question from a member of the audience.
